fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Compliance Quiz
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the quiz, the scoring, and the table of attempts from one prompt. Describe a change and it rebuilds that part.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted from your policy

Paste a policy section or the training slides, and Emergent writes scenario questions with one right answer and three plausible wrong ones. A follow-up prompt rewords any of them.
fields.feature_2:
A pass mark you choose

Set the pass mark, such as 8 of 10, and the quiz scores each attempt against it. Anyone below it gets a retake with the questions in a new order, and both attempts stay on file.
fields.feature_3:
Every attempt in a database you own

Each attempt is a row with the person's name, team, date, score, and every option they picked. The table sits in a database you own, so this year's results sit beside last year's.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders until the quiz closes

People who have not finished get an email reminder before the close date, and the compliance lead gets a Slack list of who is still out. Anyone who has finished stops getting emails.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen on a phone

Staff on a shift answer on a phone, one question per screen, and see why the right answer is right before moving on. Emergent puts no cap on responses, so every location can take it.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and code on paid plans

Run the quiz on your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository, next to your other internal tools.

fields.tab_content_1:
Gifts from vendors: 41 of 212 got it wrong

Teagarden Freight sends a 10-question code of conduct quiz to all 212 drivers and office staff each February, and 8 of 10 is a pass. Each answer is saved with the person's name and depot. The question on gifts from vendors was missed by 41 of 212, more than any other, and HR rewrote that part of next year's training.
fields.tab_content_2:
When a score is under 6 of 8, a retake link goes out

After each quarterly phishing drill, the 38 people at Fernbeck CPAs take an 8-question quiz on what the drill email got wrong. Anyone under 6 of 8 gets a retake link by email the same day, and IT lead Wren Hollaway gets an email with their names. After the March drill, 5 of 38 scored under 6 of 8.
fields.tab_content_3:
Every new cook passes before the first shift

Pinoak Kitchens runs 3 restaurants, and each new cook takes a 6-question quiz on the kitchen's own food safety rules from a phone. The kitchen manager sees the score before the cook's first shift. This spring, 24 of 27 new hires passed on the first try, and the other 3 passed on a retake.
fields.tab_content_4:
Before day one, 58 of 63 workers had passed

Varden Ridge Builders has 63 workers from 9 subcontractors on a clinic job. Each takes a 7-question site rules quiz before day one, and each pass is saved with the worker's name and company. At 6:30 each morning, superintendent Ruth Maybrook sees who has passed. On day one, 58 of 63 had, and 5 were retaking.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Compliance Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a compliance quiz that tests judgment and shows which rule to retrain, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Turn each rule into a scenario
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set the pass mark and what follows
fields.howto_step_1_des: Build each quiz around a single policy, such as the code of conduct or the rules for handling customer data, instead of the whole handbook. Results on one policy point at one section to retrain. Name the policy in your prompt, and Emergent drafts questions from it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask what someone should do, not what a term means. A supplier offers concert tickets during a contract renewal: accept, decline, or ask the manager first? A scenario tests the judgment the policy is meant to shape, and the explanation can quote the rule it comes from.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write each wrong option as a choice a busy, well-meaning employee might make, such as forwarding a strange email to a coworker to check. Drop any option nobody would pick. Keep all four options about the same length: a right answer that runs longer than the rest gives itself away.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide the pass mark before anyone starts and put it in the invitation. Then decide what a low score triggers: a retake, a short refresher, or a talk with the compliance lead. Writing that down first keeps every result handled the same way.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Test it with two people first
fields.howto_step_5_des: Have one new hire and one manager take the quiz before launch. Rewrite any question either of them reads two ways, and check that their names, scores, and chosen options land in the results table under the right policy.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Give staff 2 weeks to finish and send the link from someone they know, such as their own manager. Remind anyone still out a week before the close and again the day before, then stop as soon as they finish.
fields.howto_step_7_des: When the quiz closes, sort the questions by how many people got them wrong. Fix that part of the training, not only the wording of the question, and ask the same question next round to see whether fewer people miss it.

faq_plan.a: A compliance quiz is a short test that checks whether employees understood a workplace rule after training, like a gifts policy or the rules for reporting phishing. Each question has one correct answer. The scores show who needs a retake, and the most-missed question shows which rule to teach again.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a compliance quiz?
faq_plan.a: Name the policy, the number of questions, and the pass mark, and Emergent's AI survey builder writes the compliance quiz along with the table that stores every attempt. Add deadline reminders or a missed-question report with a follow-up prompt, then send staff the link.

faq_plan.q: Where can I find compliance quiz questions and answers for my employees?
faq_plan.a: Write them from your own policies instead of borrowing a generic set. Each answer should then match a written rule in your handbook. The 8 sample questions on this page show the format, each tied to a US government source. Paste a policy into Emergent, and it drafts a question for each rule.

faq_plan.q: Should compliance quiz questions test scenarios or definitions?
faq_plan.a: Mostly scenarios. A question about what to do when a supplier offers concert tickets tests the judgment a policy asks for, while a definition question works like a vocabulary quiz and only checks recall. Keep definitions for the few terms staff must name correctly, such as retaliation.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a compliance quiz have?
faq_plan.a: About 10 per policy: one for each rule that matters, and short enough to finish on a break. Split a long handbook into several short quizzes instead of one 40-question test, and each set of results will point at one policy.

faq_plan.q: What passing score should a compliance quiz use?
faq_plan.a: Start at 8 of 10 unless you have a reason to pick another number, and raise it for rules where one mistake is costly, such as handling customer data. State the mark in the invitation; nobody should learn it after failing.

faq_plan.q: Can a compliance quiz be fun without losing the point?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the humor lives in the scenarios and the answer options stay plain. A story about an intern who almost pays a fake invoice holds attention, and the correct choice is still clear. Save pure jokes for funny survey questions, where no score depends on them.

faq_plan.q: How often should employees retake a compliance quiz?
faq_plan.a: Run it after each training round and again when the policy changes. If a regulator, insurer, or client contract sets a schedule, follow that schedule. Between rounds, ask last round's most-missed questions again to see whether the training fixed them.

faq_plan.q: How do I track who passed a compliance quiz?
faq_plan.a: Save each attempt with the name, date, score, and chosen options, then filter by score. A quiz built on Emergent keeps those rows in a database you own, and a follow-up prompt adds a page listing everyone who has not passed yet.

faq_plan.q: Can each department get its own compliance quiz questions?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Open with a question that asks for the department, then show each one its own set: drivers answer questions on logbooks, and finance answers on expense approvals. A style quiz uses the same kind of answer-based branching to pick a result.

quiz.title: Workplace Compliance Quiz: 8 Questions on the Basics
quiz.intro: Eight questions on harassment, retaliation, safety, security, and bribery rules, each answered from a US government source. Your score and the reasons show at the end.

questions.text: Under EEOC guidance, harassment based on older age covers workers starting at what age?
questions.explanation: The EEOC lists older age, beginning at age 40, among the bases for harassment, next to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, and genetic information.

source.quote: Harassment is unwelcome conduct that is based on race, color, religion, sex (including sexual orientation, transgender status, or pregnancy), national origin, older age (beginning at age 40), disability, or genetic information

questions.text: Under EEOC guidance, when does offensive conduct at work become unlawful harassment?

options.text: When it is severe or pervasive enough to create a hostile workplace
Only when a manager is the one doing it
Only after the employee complains in writing
Only when it happens three or more times

questions.explanation: The EEOC names two cases: putting up with the conduct becomes a condition of keeping the job, or it is severe or pervasive enough that a reasonable person would find the workplace hostile.

source.quote: Harassment becomes unlawful where 1) enduring the offensive conduct becomes a condition of continued employment, or 2) the conduct is severe or pervasive enough to create a work environment that a reasonable person would consider intimidating, hostile, or abusive

questions.text: An employee files a discrimination complaint, and her manager changes her schedule on purpose to punish her for it. What could that be?
questions.explanation: The EEOC gives this example of what could be retaliation, depending on the facts: punishing an employee for a complaint by changing their work schedule on purpose.

source.quote: punishing an employee for an EEO complaint by purposefully changing his work schedule

questions.text: OSHA says workers have the right to safety and health training in which language?
questions.explanation: OSHA lists it among every worker's rights: workplace safety and health training in a language the worker understands.

source.quote: Receive workplace safety and health training in a language you understand

questions.text: A worker thinks the workplace is unsafe. What can they file with OSHA?

options.text: A confidential complaint asking OSHA to inspect
Only a complaint signed and shared with the employer
Only a complaint passed on by a manager

questions.explanation: OSHA says a worker who thinks a workplace is unsafe or unhealthy can file a confidential complaint and ask OSHA to inspect it.

source.quote: you can file a confidential complaint with OSHA and ask them to inspect it

questions.text: An email says your account closes today unless you act right now. CISA tells businesses to train staff to treat urgent language as what?

options.text: Proof the email came from IT
A sign it passed the spam filter

questions.explanation: CISA advises training employees to watch for red flags such as strange or unexpected requests, urgent language, or suspicious links.

source.quote: Train employees to watch for red flags such as strange or unexpected requests, urgent language or suspicious links

questions.text: Per CISA, how many ways to verify a user's identity does multifactor authentication (MFA) require?
questions.explanation: CISA describes MFA as an extra layer of protection that requires two or more ways to verify who is signing in.

source.quote: adds an extra layer of protection by requiring two or more ways to verify a user

questions.text: Under the FCPA's anti-bribery rules, what can count as a bribe to a foreign official?
questions.explanation: The Justice Department describes the rules as covering an offer, payment, or promise of money or anything of value meant to influence a foreign official.

source.quote: authorization of the payment of money or anything of value to any person

results.title: Time for a Refresher
results.description: You got 3 or fewer right. Read the explanations below, then find the matching section of your company's policy for each one you missed. Those sections are a good place to start your next training round.

results.title: Solid Footing
results.description: You got between 4 and 6 right. The basics are there, and the misses below show the gaps. Look at which topics they fall under, such as safety or phishing, and reread that part of your policy first.

results.title: Sharp on the Basics
results.description: You got 7 or 8 right. You know where these rules come from and what they cover. Check the explanations for any question you guessed, and try writing one scenario question of your own.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Compliance Quiz That Shows Each Missed Rule' and hero carry the primary's whole job; hero description 122 chars, leads with 'Take the 8-question compliance quiz below, or build a compliance quiz that saves each score and answer to a table you own.'; how-to description one sentence under 140 chars with the primary.

intent.evidence: Secondaries show searchers want real questions with answers; the page delivers a playable 8-question quiz with answers, explanations and US government sources, then the build-your-own path with pass marks, retakes and a results table. Title promise '8 Questions, Then Build Yours' and meta 'free 8-question compliance quiz on harassment, safety, and phishing' are both delivered on the page.

specificity.evidence: Every section speaks compliance-training vocabulary: pass mark 8 of 10, retake links, most-missed question, code of conduct, phishing drill, site rules before day one. Table generated from the library (vs SurveyMonkey, Microsoft Forms, SurveyHero); why_description is page-specific: 'Every attempt keeps the options a person picked, in tables you own.'

openers.evidence: All feature bodies open on verbs or full sentences ('Paste a policy section or the training slides, and Emergent writes...'); tabs open on company actions ('Teagarden Freight sends...', 'After each quarterly phishing drill...'); how-to steps open on actions. No keyword labels or fragments.

craft.evidence: Sentences vary in length and end on the load-bearing word ('a right answer that runs longer than the rest gives itself away'). Two ', so' endings and topic-word repetition accepted as notes below; nothing at blocking level.

voice.evidence: Concrete, unglamorous detail throughout (41 of 212 missed the gifts question, retake link the same day, 6:30 list for Ruth Maybrook); no hype verbs, no triplet rhythm, no summary sentences. Would ship unedited.

truth.evidence: All 7 claims_used ids are approved (prompt-build, database-owned, alerts, conversational, no-caps, custom-domain, code-export); GitHub export correctly scoped to paid plans. Quiz Z4 flags checked by hand: each quoted span states the correct answer (q2 'severe or pervasive enough to create a work environment... hostile'; q3 EEOC retaliation schedule-change example; q4 'in a language you understand'; q5 'file a confidential complaint with OSHA and ask them to inspect it'; q6 'red flags such as... urgent language'). All 6 source URLs are EEOC/OSHA/CISA/DOJ primary sources, sources-check ok. Cross-field numbers agree everywhere: 212/41/8-of-10, 38=14+19+5, 27=24+3, 63=58+5.

distinct.evidence: Four tabs are four distinct real segments (freight code of conduct, CPA phishing drill, restaurant food safety, construction site rules); no sibling primary in any heading; playable sourced quiz is an angle no sibling carries. Two template-slot echoes of the board-survey exemplar recorded as repeated-idea notes.

faq.evidence: 10 real on-topic questions, each answered in its first sentence; both secondaries carried naturally ('Where can I find compliance quiz questions and answers for my employees?', 'Should compliance quiz questions test scenarios or definitions?'); hub link in item 2, 3 sibling links (vocabulary quiz, funny survey questions, style quiz) with exact-match anchors; 2 moat lines in items 3 and 9, subtle and claim-safe; no brands, no file formats; verbatim check: no AlsoAsked items, all written.

images.evidence: Contact sheet read: each tab matches its copy word for word on names, numbers and outcomes (Teagarden 212/10q/41 missed/19%; Fernbeck 38=14+19+5, email to Wren Hollaway, retake same day; Pinoak phone quiz Q3 of 6, 24 of 27 first try; Varden Ridge 63/9 subs, 6:30 list for Ruth Maybrook, 58 passed + 5 retaking). One hero per tab, cursor on button edges, panels full, text readable; alert drawn as email to the named person, not a channel; percentages recompute correctly; fictional names clean, 'Retaking' status not mapped onto ethnicity or gender; cover is a confirm screen, OG matches the pitch.
